docRequirement: `whats-new/2026-w29.md:63` binds us to a session-wide WebSearch budget: "Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`". Two other snapshot pages give the semantics of the WebSearch half exactly. `env-vars.md:283`: "Cap on the total number of WebSearch calls one session can make (default: 200). When Claude reaches the cap, further WebSearch calls return a notice telling it to continue with the information it already gathered. Accepts a positive whole number with no upper bound. Anything else is ignored and the default applies, so the cap can be raised but not turned off." `tools-reference.md:432`: "A session can make at most 200 WebSearch calls, counted across the main conversation and every subagent it spawns, so searches made by parallel research fan-outs count against the same limit… When Claude reaches the limit, further calls return a notice telling Claude to continue with the information it already gathered, rather than an error that would invite a retry. You don't see the notice." So: one counter per session TREE (parent + every subagent), default 200, raisable-not-disablable via one env knob, and the over-cap result is a non-error notice, invisible to the user.
current: The tool exists and is unbudgeted. `createSearchTool` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.ts:56-114) returns the `web_search` ToolDefinition (`name: 'web_search'` at :61); its `execute` (:68-112) clamps only the per-call result `count` to 1-10 (:70) and then calls `provider.search` unconditionally (:73), with a single fallback attempt (:81). There is no counter, no default, no env read in the file. It is registered unconditionally into `webTools` at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1393-1396, and that same array instance is spread into both tool projections (:1517, :1786), so every turn of the session sees the same unbudgeted definition. packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:256 binds it to Claude's `WebSearch` (`binding('web_search', 'web_search', 'web_search', 'web_search', 'WebSearch')`), so this is the surface the page is about. No knob exists under either spelling: `grep -ra` over packages/ apps/ for `MAX_WEB_SEARCHES`, `SEARCHES_PER`, `WEB_SEARCH_PER`, `webSearchLimit`, `searchBudget`, `webSearchCount`, `searchCallCount`, `sessionCap`, `callBudget` returns no source hits (only this sweep's own docs). Nothing one layer up absorbs it: the spawner bounds depth (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110, enforced :519-521) and simultaneity (`Semaphore`, :204-208, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16` at :103), and the per-child `budgets` it ships (:600-608 → `PiChildBudgetsV1`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:6-15) carry depth/fanout/concurrency/tokenLimit/costLimitUsd/deadlineAt/ancestry and no search count. `orchestrator.maxAgents` (default 1000, packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49) is per workflow run, not per session, and never reaches `web_search`. The cross-subagent clause is structurally unreachable today: a subagent is a full separate session (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10391 `startPiChildRuntime` → `createSession`, driven by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:53), so each child runs its own pi-agent-server subprocess with its own `createSearchTool` instance and would not share any in-process counter.
divergence: The whole mechanism is missing — this is not a wrong key name or a wrong default. Three separate pieces are absent: (1) any per-session count of `web_search` calls; (2) the 200 default and its env lever (our spelling would be `NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION`, per this repo's documented rename convention at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:9-12); (3) the documented over-cap RESULT — a non-error notice telling the model to continue with what it has. Note the shape of (3): our failure path already returns `details: { isError: true }` (create-search-tool.ts:97, :109), and the cap must NOT use it, because the page explicitly contrasts the notice with "an error that would invite a retry". One further scope gap beyond the mechanism itself: because subagents are separate sessions/subprocesses, a counter that is merely per-process satisfies the default and the knob but not `tools-reference.md:432`'s "counted across the main conversation and every subagent it spawns" — a parallel research fan-out would get one full budget per child.

change.what: New file, modelled on the two existing precedents: the env-rename header of packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:1-13 and the knob parser of packages/shared/src/structured-output/retry.ts:12-37. Export `DEFAULT_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION = 200`, `MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION_ENV = 'NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION'`, and `resolveMaxWebSearchesPerSession(env: Record<string, string|undefined> = process.env): number` that accepts ONLY plain digits — `/^\d+$/` on the trimmed value, parsed and required > 0 — and returns the default for anything else. Two deliberate differences from retry.ts: no ceiling clamp (`env-vars.md:283` says "no upper bound"), and no per-call override, because the cap is not per call. Also export a tiny counter seam `createWebSearchBudget(limit: number, alreadyUsed = 0)` returning `{ limit, used(): number, tryConsume(): boolean }` so the enforcement point is unit-testable without a provider. Header comment must carry the mapping `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` → `NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` and cite `env-vars.md:283` + `tools-reference.md:432` verbatim, the way background-task-settings.ts:9-12 does. ~35 lines.

Add a third parameter `options?: { budget?: WebSearchBudget }` (keep it optional so the five existing test call sites and the two harness-contract fixtures keep compiling unchanged). At the top of `execute` (:68-70), BEFORE the provider call at :73, do `if (options?.budget && !options.budget.tryConsume()) return notice(...)`. `notice()` returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: <notice> }], details: {} }` — deliberately WITHOUT `isError`, unlike the two failure returns at :90-99 and :102-110; `tools-reference.md:432` requires a notice "rather than an error that would invite a retry". Text must tell the model to continue with what it already gathered and name the lever, e.g. `Web search limit reached for this session (<limit> searches). Continue with the information you already gathered; if you genuinely need more searches, ask the user to raise NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION.` Consume exactly once per `execute` call, before the primary attempt, so the internal fallback attempt (:81) does not double-count and a provider failure still spends the call (the doc counts "WebSearch calls", not successes). ~12 lines.

Create ONE budget for the process at module scope (not inside `buildSessionDefinition`, which is called a second time for the cwd-prepare candidate at :2951 — a per-closure counter would silently reset on a working-directory switch) and pass it: `createSearchTool(searchProvider, undefined, { budget: webSearchBudget })`. Seed it from `resolveMaxWebSearchesPerSession()`; the knob already reaches this process because PiAgent spawns it with `...process.env` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1462-1477). Do NOT put the cap on `InitMessage.orchestrator` (:232-244): that object is normalized into the signed manifest identity (`expectedOrchestrator: normalizePiOrchestratorConfig(...)` at :1531 and :1793), and the README's `maxParallelTasks` row (packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:47) records what adding a per-host number there costs — a manifest/model-contract mismatch that kills the first turn. ~6 lines.

The cross-subagent half, and the only part that crosses a boundary. Because each subagent is its own session and subprocess (SessionManager.ts:10391 → createSession), the count must be host-owned per session TREE. Recommended shape: add one optional field `webSearchesUsed?: number` to `InitMessage` (a JSONL-only shape — do NOT touch `orchestrator`), seed the subprocess budget with it, and report consumption back to the host on the existing result/event channel; the host keeps the running total on the root session and passes the current value into every `PiChildStartInput` it starts, resolving the root through the existing `budgets.ancestry` (child-session-port.ts:6-15). Adding a numeric field to `PiChildBudgetsV1` is the alternative and is the more invasive one: that interface is part of the persisted `PiChildSessionRecordV1`/`PiChildSessionStateV1` (child-session-port.ts:60-101, `schemaVersion: 1`, written by `ChildSessionService.persist`), so it is a persistence-schema change. Either way a parallel fan-out can overshoot by up to the number of children started before their first report settles; record that as the accepted narrowing. If the plan chooses to ship enforcement per pi-subprocess ONLY, this entry is dropped, effort falls to M, and the narrowing ("one budget per session and per subagent, not one per tree") must be written into the audit row rather than left implicit.

Two representative cases plus a table for the parser (the repo's minimum-non-duplicative rule): (1) with a budget of 1, the second `execute` returns the notice, `details.isError` is undefined, and the provider's `search` was called exactly once — the negative path AND the proof the provider is not reached; (2) a provider failure still consumes one unit (so a failing search cannot loop for free). Parser table in a new packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/web-search-budget.test.ts: unset → 200, `'50'` → 50, `'0'`/`'-1'`/`'abc'`/`'1e3'`/`'1_000'`/`' 50 '` → per the digits-only rule (`env-vars.md:283`: "this variable doesn't take the scientific notation or digit-separator spellings" is stated for the sibling subagent knob; keep the same reader for both so they cannot drift).

Document the `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` → `NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` mapping the way fork-subagents.md:32 documents `NESSY_FORK_SUBAGENT`, and add/close the audit row for this page (f236 plus its sibling f235/f085/f132 for the subagent half). Then regenerate the two generated files per AGENTS.md: `python3 scripts/build-parity-report.py > docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-parity-report.md` and `python3 scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py > docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md`.

blastRadius: Readers of `createSearchTool`: one production call site (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1394, whose array is reused at :1517 and :1786) and five test/fixture call sites — packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.test.ts, src/session-tool-registration.test.ts:67,:120,:131, src/harness/live-manifest-contract.test.ts:110, src/__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:158,:292,:687. Keeping the new parameter optional keeps all of them green. The harness-contract ledger pins `web_search` in packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/fixtures/tool-surface.json (rows :561 and :1670); its `handlerSchemaVersion` is `<path>#createSearchTool.execute@<commit sha>` and the assertion only checks `toContain('#<handlerName>@')` (pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:107, :501), so editing the body is safe but RENAMING the file or the function would break the pin. The tool result text enters the model transcript and the tool-call UI, so the notice wording is user-visible surface even though the doc says the user does not see it as an error. `harness-tool-descriptor.ts:256` is the `web_search`→`WebSearch` binding any permission/deny rule resolves through — unchanged by this work, but it is why this tool is the contract surface. WIRE/PERSISTENCE: the cross-subagent counter crosses the pi-agent-server JSONL protocol (`InboundMessage`/`InitMessage`, whose shape has source-marker pins in packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/pi-runtime-protocol.test.ts:75-96) and, if `PiChildBudgetsV1` is chosen as the carrier, the PERSISTED `PiChildSessionRecordV1`/`PiChildSessionStateV1` (`schemaVersion: 1`) written by `ChildSessionService` — both are risk triggers under this repo's verification policy. `InitMessage.orchestrator` must stay untouched: it feeds `normalizePiOrchestratorConfig` into the signed manifest identity at index.ts:1531/:1793/:2758. Out of scope and not fixed by this: the Claude Agent SDK backend (`NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`, off by default) carries whatever caps Anthropic ships, and the Codex runtime's own web search is inside the vendored `codex-app-server` binary (its protocol type is packages/codex-protocol/generated/WebSearchToolConfig.ts) which we cannot budget from here.
userImpact: None observable in ordinary use — no wrong output, no missing UI. It surfaces the moment a turn loops on search, which is exactly the case the cap exists for, and there is no backstop at all: the model can issue unlimited `web_search` calls in one session, and a `subagent` fan-out multiplies that with no shared ceiling. Two concrete consequences. On the default Nessy Gateway/Pi connection the provider is DuckDuckGo, so a loop hammers three DDG endpoints with up to three retries each (packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/providers/ddg.ts:38-59, :202-227); DDG answers with its anomaly/"too quickly" throttle, so the user watches searches get slower and then start failing, with each failure feeding a `Search failed…` block into context instead of a notice telling the model to stop and use what it has. On an OpenAI-API-key, ChatGPT-subscription or Google-key connection every single call is a billed upstream request (packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/resolve-provider.ts:58-86, providers/chatgpt.ts:100-110), so the same loop spends real quota or money with nothing to stop it. What would make it visible deliberately: a research prompt that keeps searching, or a `subagent` fan-out of research agents — today each child gets its own unlimited budget.
